CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with a past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc who presents for her annual exam. She reports that her herniated disc has been doing well since a steroid injection several months ago, with no back pain or limitations in movement. Her carpal tunnel release, performed a couple of years ago, has also been doing well with no recurrent issues, full range of motion, and she has returned to work with no numbness and tingling in her hands. Regarding her coronary artery disease, over the last month she has been having chest pain that occurs when she walks and resolves with rest. She denies chest pain at rest. She describes the pain as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest, occurring approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. She states the pain is not severe enough to warrant an emergency room visit but she does notice it.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses chest pain as described above and nasal congestion from allergies due to pollen. She denies lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever, or chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Prior carpal tunnel release
Herniated disc

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently working.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygenation normal. Heart: Slight 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur. Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no carotid bruits appreciated. Extremities: No lower extremity edema. Surgical scars noted on right wrist, well healed.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from last year: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%, mild mitral regurgitation.
EKG: Stable, reflects prior coronary artery disease, no new changes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Carpal tunnel release: Patient doing well, no further intervention needed at this time. Patient to report if recurrent symptoms occur.
Herniated disc: Patient doing well, no further steroid injection or physical therapy needed at this time. Patient to report if recurrent symptoms occur.
Coronary artery disease with recurrent chest pain: Continue aspirin and toprol. Order cardiac stress test to evaluate for additional blockages. Obtain lipid panel. Start crestor 20 mg once daily.
